Fight Forward Pass

How a buddy thinks in a fight: everything that has happened so far, run through the same fixed weights every moment, to find where every character's health is heading and which answer bends it toward victory. Issue 625n.

The idea

A language model reads everything said so far through fixed weights and scores every word it could say next. A buddy reads the fight so far through fixed weights and scores every answer it could give now. The pieces line up one to one.

A language modelA buddy in a fight
Everything said so farThe fight so far: one snapshot and a minute of events

The snapshot

Taken by the world thread when something has happened (no thinking while nothing does, issue 627; at most every half second in combat), once per party, so every buddy reads the same picture. Plain values copied, never game objects, so worker threads can read it while the game moves on. Buddies see every number for now; equalizing what they are shown against what a player beside them could see is the later goal.

A minute of events

Each hit, heal, mark landing or wearing off, cast and death goes into a ring that holds the last minute, each stamped with its time. Running summaries are updated as each event arrives, so a step never reads the whole minute again: damage taken and healing received per second for each character, damage dealt per second against each enemy, each enemy's health trend (which is the fight-length guess, already built).

The weights

Mostly fixed. Three kinds:

  1. The game's own tables, read by generators: every class's abilities, what each buff gives, which talents touch which abilities, the lockouts (Forbearance, Sated), the threat levers. Still to add: what each debuff does to whoever carries it.
  2. Each buddy's own: its abilities, talents and gear, worked out again when they change.
  3. The few that may move with play, each kept with where it started and how it moves: how much a talent benefits an ability, how a rating relates to a spell, how resistant a target is to a school, how much mana matters in this fight.

The six layers

Each step runs them in order, each reading the one before.

  1. Rates built, offline
    Health lost and gained per character, enemies' health falling, so the fight's time left. (625h)
  2. Marks to modifiers built, offline
    Every buff and debuff a multiplier on damage taken, healing received, damage dealt, haste, speed, ticks, absorbs and armour, ending when it does; empowering buffs already up as windows. (625n)
  3. Attention built, offline
    Whom each enemy attacks now and next, in the server's own order. (625j)
  4. Fight curves built, offline
    Each character's health to the fight's end, by who holds the attention, marks wearing off, and enemies' casts landing as lumps. (625j)
  5. Plans part built
    Each buddy's long cooldowns lined up (lockouts counted), the tanks' swaps; the healer's plan and who gets each buff still to come. (625f 625i 625l)
  6. Answers built, offline
    Each answer a buddy could give now, tried as if given; its lean the share of the gap it closes (health first, then the group's time), handed to the draw. (625n)

New, extended, desired

  • New is the snapshot just taken.
  • Extended is the fight curves carried forward to the fight's end, with the plans in them.
  • Desired is what the group values: victory first (every enemy dead before anyone in the party, no curve below nothing); then, by default, fewer consumables used and a faster kill; when questing, gold and experience per hour.

Each step measures the gap from extended to desired. An answer is worth what it closes of that gap, said in damage and health so everything adds up.

Fight curves, by hand

A tank at 2000 of 8000 health, a fury warrior and a priest behind it. Move the numbers and pick a lever; the curves are each character's health to the fight's end, worked out the way the buddy module works them out. The starting values are the ones its test checks: nothing done leaves the party 4000 short, Lay on Hands none, Hand of Protection with the fury warrior next 1700, with the priest next worse than nothing.

tankfury warriorpriestthe band under the chart: who holds the attention

Where it runs

The world thread only takes the snapshot and reads the last verdict; the game's objects are safe to touch only there. A pool of worker threads runs the layers: one task per party for what is shared (attention, the fight curves, the tanks' swaps, who gets each buff), one per buddy for its own plan and answers. Verdicts are double-buffered: the workers write the next while the bot module reads the last, at most one step old. Measured: a buddy's cooldown plan takes about half a millisecond for a five-minute fight, a fight curve microseconds.

Calm, and replays

The server's own switching margins (a new attacker must beat the current one by a tenth in melee reach, three tenths at range), no swap or hold for nothing, weights that change smoothly, and the weighted draw at the end keep the buddies natural rather than scripted. Every step's snapshot and verdict can be written to a log; a recorded fight run back through the layers gives the same verdicts every time, so changes are tested on real fights and learning has its material.

The owner's words

The idea

okay so the curve is a path through a series of weights, sorta like when an LLM is processing a long string of output text. At the instant when it processes it's next token, it feeds all the previous data through the same weights and sees where it trajectorizes to. We want to do something similar, all of the status effects of the fight should be charted and mapped and routed through these weights, each moment we supply the entire state and it updates the fight curve according to the new, and extended, and desired, state.

What is desired

depends on the group. What do they value? besides victory, bots prefer lower gold cost (use fewer consumables) and faster time (3 minute kill instead of 4). When questing and such, they prefer things like gold-per-hour, and exp-per-hour.

What a buddy may know

we can let them know. Yes, it's not human, but humans have better capabilities in some ways and worse in others. So, with an eventual goal of equalizing the presented information, let's just let them see the numbers for now.

How far back

a minute is fine.

The weights

I don't imagine they will grow very much. They are things like, how much certain talents benefit certain abilities, how critical strike rating relates to certain spells, how resistant a target is to a certain type of shadow blast, how important mana is to this particular fight, stuff like that.

Still open

Gold cost: which consumables count (potions, food, flasks, reagents, ammunition, repairs), and is each counted at its vendor price, or at the auction house's when there is one?
